question:
At the end of each release our bug tracker tells us only how many bugs were found, and that count gives the team nothing to act on. What should we do with our bug records so that they help us introduce fewer bugs in later releases?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

Bug counts alone are insufficient to prevent recurrence. Teams should classify defects into meaningful taxonomies, record and store defect data, perform root cause analysis, apply statistical and trend analysis, develop defect profiles, and implement corrective and preventive actions to continuously improve software engineering processes and reduce future bugs.

# Guidelines

- Classify defects into a meaningful taxonomy rather than counting numbers alone, since numbers without classification are insufficient to identify underlying causes and prevent recurrence. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Quality Metrics, Reliability Models, and Corrective Actions/Corrective and Preventive Actions in Quality Management.md)

- Establish a defect classification taxonomy and record all defect data found during SQA, since data on errors and defects may be lost unless they are recorded. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Software Quality Management and Defect Classification.md)

- Perform root cause analysis (RCA) on defect records to find root causes and use measurement techniques to improve software engineering processes, techniques, and tools. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Software Quality Management and Defect Classification.md)

- Use defect density, error density, and failure rate measurements to build defect profiles for the application domain, then use those profiles in the next project to focus effort where problems are most likely to occur. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Quality Metrics, Reliability Models, and Corrective Actions/Software Quality Measurements and Reliability Models.md)

- Apply statistical and trend analysis techniques such as Pareto analysis, control charts, and run charts to identify the most troublesome defect areas and focus corrective process improvements where most needed. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Measurement and Analysis Techniques/Software Quality Measurement and Statistical Analysis Techniques.md)

- Use RCA techniques such as 5-whys, cause-and-effect diagrams, and change analysis to discover sources of recurring defects and reveal opportunities for software process improvement. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Standards, Quality Assurance, and Modern Manufacturing Systems/Root Cause Analysis Methods and Application/Root Cause Analysis Techniques.md)

- Select corrective actions that prevent recurrence, are within the organization's control, and meet organizational goals; implement them and observe their efficiency and effectiveness. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Standards, Quality Assurance, and Modern Manufacturing Systems/Industry 4.0 and Software Engineering Integration.md)

- Use fault type classification and statistics from past projects to make quality predictions and guide process improvement in future projects. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/SUT Measurements and Fault Classification for Test Planning.md)

- Document and record test incidents in a problem reporting system so the data can serve as the basis for debugging, fixing, and identifying which [SWEBOK excerpt 02251924d460790fdb0d]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Test Generation, Environment Setup, and Incident Management/Test Incident Reporting and Documentation Process.md)

- Use [SWEBOK excerpt df027194885f5813d595] as a source of information for error guessing in future test design. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Testing Approaches and Execution Strategies/Software Testing Techniques and Methodologies/Experience-Based Techniques for Test Suite Generation.md)

- Document corrective actions and submit them so the quality management system is improved to prevent problems from recurring in future software projects. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Quality Metrics, Reliability Models, and Corrective Actions/Corrective and Preventive Actions in Quality Management.md)

- Update the organization's measurement database with relevant project defect data and conduct retrospective analysis so lessons learned feed into organizational learning and improvement. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Software Engineering Measurement and Organizational Learning.md)

- Ensure every metric collected supports an actual decision; avoid gathering defect data merely because it is easy to measure, as measurements not used to support any decision are a waste of time and energy. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Measurement Scales, Reliability, and Practical Application/Measurement Reliability and Decision-Driven Metrics/Measurement Purpose and Avoiding Wasteful Metrics.md)
